disease_label_per_paper: Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli (STEC)-associated hemolytic uremic syndrome in an adult with advanced ovarian cancer receiving neoadjuvant chemotherapy
presentation_summary: 55-year-old woman with known advanced (FIGO IIIC) high-grade serous ovarian cancer was hospitalized after the first cycle of neoadjuvant paclitaxel/carboplatin with acute abdominal pain and bloody diarrhea.
Abdominal CT: ascites with peritoneal deposits, enlarged right ovary, omental caking, circumferential bowel wall thickening with marked submucosal edema.

Despite aggressive IV fluids she became oliguric; labs before nephrology transfer: CRP 82.6 mg/L, WBC 18.4 x10^9/L (neutrophils 78%), Hb 125 g/L, platelets 114 x10^9/L, creatinine 250 umol/L, BUN 16.3 mmol/L, LDH 18.81 ukat/L, AST 0.83, ALT 0.52, GGT 1.00 ukat/L, schistocytes 0.5%, Na 127.7 mmol/L, K 4.32, Cl 99.9.
No presentation vital signs were reported.
snapshot_note: Snapshot = initial hospital evaluation before transfer to nephrology (paper's Table 1 labs, CT, and oliguria). No separate earlier admission lab set is reported.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Stool multiplex PCR (FilmArray gastrointestinal panel) detected STEC
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Multiplex polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing of a stool sample (FilmArray gastrointestinal panel; BioFire Diagnostics, Salt Lake City, Utah, USA) detected STEC

confirmatory_findings.finding: Final diagnosis per paper: STEC-associated HUS (not chemotherapy-induced TMA)
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: The temporal relationship in this case, together with classical STEC-HUS laboratory and clinical findings, strongly supports Shiga toxin-mediated endothelial injury as the primary cause.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Residential water supply contamination identified by later sanitary inspection
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Notably, local sanitary inspection identified contamination of the patient's residential water supply around the time of STEC infection.

clinical_course_events.finding: Later in the nephrology admission: fever and hypotension with Enterobacter cloacae complex bacteremia
clinical_course_events.source_text_value: During this period, fever and hypotension developed, and antibiotic therapy with ciprofloxacin and metronidazole was initiated following positive blood cultures for Enterobacter cloacae complex.

actual_treatment: nine units packed red blood cells, albumin, platelet transfusions
ciprofloxacin and metronidazole for later Enterobacter cloacae complex bacteremia
later carboplatin monotherapy and cytoreductive surgery

outcome.source_text_value: She was eventually discharged in stable condition. ... Despite these interventions, she died several months later due to disease progression.

quality_warnings: No vital signs at presentation were reported.

Peritoneal deposits, omental caking, enlarged ovary, and possibly ascites reflect the pre-existing stage IIIC ovarian cancer; they are presentation CT findings and are kept rankable, with the malignancy also recorded in risk_context.
BUN was reported in mmol/L with a urea-type reference range; converted to mg/dL urea nitrogen with factor 2.8.
Enzyme values reported in ukat/L were converted with factor 60 to U/L.
Stool STEC PCR, later bacteremia, treatment, and outcome are non-ranking.
